<entry id="O00918">
<head-word>סָכַם</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (cmp. סָכָה) 
<italic>to look to, take in view</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Macc. III, 10 (22
<sup>a</sup>) (ref. to במספר Deut. XXV, 3, combined with ארבעים of next verse) מנין שהוא סוֹכֵם את הארבעים Ms. M. (ed. שהוא סמוך לארב') a number which faces (is matched in counting with) forty, (i.e. thirty nine); ib. 22
<sup>b</sup>; Yalk. Deut. 937 סמוך את וכ'; Yalk. Zech. 581 סוכם; Sifré Deut. 286 סמוך לארב'.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִסְכִּים</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to contemplate, plan</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Midr. Till. to Ps. LXXIII, 7 (ref. to משכיות, ib.) יש שהיה מַסְכִּים וכ' (ed. Bub. מַשְׂכִּים) one planned to become a centurio, and thou madest him a general &c.; על כל מה שהיו מַסְכִּימִים העברת וכ' thou didst carry them beyond all they ever contemplated (to become).</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition> (cmp. חָשַׁב, שָׁוָה) 
<italic>to harmonize; to agree</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Sifra Vayikra, N’dab., ch. IV, Par. 4 ואתה דורש ומַסְכִּים לשמועה and thou interpretest the text and harmonizest it with the traditional law; Yalk. Lev. 440 ומסכים הלכה and harmonizest the tradition (with the text). Yeb. 62
<sup>a</sup> והִסְכִּימָה דעתו לדעת וכ' and his (Moses’) opinion (the result of his deliberations) turned out to be in agreement with the Lord’s; Sabb. 87
<sup>a</sup> וה' הקב"ה עמו the Lord agreed with him; ib. ה' הקב"ה על ידו the Lord approved his doing; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<sup>a</sup> top דלית הוא מַסְכְּמָה עימיה that he did not share his opinion; a. e.—Part. pass. מַסְכַּם; f. מַסְכְּמָא. Lam. R. to I, 2 הא חסילה והא מ' ע"י וכ' it is made final and confirmed by Jeremiah.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>

<entry id="O00923">
<head-word>סָכַן</head-word>
<hw-number>II</hw-number>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<language-reference>
<xref rid="O00910"> cmp. סָכַל II)</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> , 
<italic>Pi.</italic> סִכֵּן 
<italic>to be perplexed; to despair; to be in danger</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ber. I, 3 וסִכַּנְתִּי בעצמי וכ' and I despaired of my life on account of robbers (whom I met there); Y. ib. 3
<sup>b</sup> bot. וסִיכַּ'. Men. 64
<sup>b</sup> בזוב סִיכְּנָה, v. זוֹב; בעינה ס' she was in danger of losing her eye-sight; בים ס' she was in danger of drowning in the sea.—Part. pass. מְסוּכָּן; f. מְסוּכֶּנֶת q. v.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hithpa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִסְתַּכֵּן</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to become confused, to be misled;</italic></definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be exposed to danger</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Tosef. Meg. I, 3; Meg. 2
<sup>a</sup> Var. הואיל ומִסְתַּכְּנִין בה, v. סָכַל II; Y. ib. I, 70
<sup>d</sup> במקום שנכנסין וכ' (read: שמסתכנין, or שנִסְכָּנִין, 
<italic>Nif.</italic>) where people might be misled, they must read the M’gillah on the fourteenth; ר' יוסי בעי אם במקום שנכנסין אל יקראו וכ' (correct as above) R. José (taking מסתכנין in the sense of being in danger) objected, if danger to life is connected with reading the M’gillah, let them not read it at all.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<entry id="O00924">
<head-word>סְכֵן</head-word>
<head-word>סְכֵין</head-word>
<language-key>ch.</language-key>
<language-reference>same</language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition />
<notes> Y. Shebi. IV, 35
<sup>b</sup> top וסכין and got himself into trouble. Y. Ab. Zar. II, 40
<sup>d</sup> bot. רחם … וס' fell in love with a woman …, and became dangerously ill.; Y. Sabb. XIV, 14
<sup>d</sup> bot. Y. Ab. Zar. l. c. ומשתי ולא יִסְכַּן and let him drink it, that he may not get ill. Y. Shek. V, 48
<sup>d</sup> בעינה סַכְנַת she was in danger of losing her eye-sight; בימה ס' she was in danger of drowning &c., 
<pgbrk id="pg992" />v. 
<xref rid="O00923">preced.</xref> Y. Ab. Zar. III, 42
<sup>c</sup> וסַכְנָן נפשתא (not וסכנתן) human lives were in danger; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>סַכֵּין</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to expose to danger; to hurt; to mislead, bring into trouble</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ber. 25
<sup>b</sup> סַכַּנְתּוּן לברי you might have brought my son into trouble (by causing him to sin unawares). Sabb. 116
<sup>a</sup> בעו לסַכּוּנֵיה they tried to give him trouble; a. fr.—Part. pass. מְסַכַּן; f. מְסַכְּנָא. Targ. II Sam. XXII, 5.—Y. Peah VIII, 21
<sup>a</sup> top עד דהוא מצמית לון הוא מס' until he gets them together for a meeting, he might be in danger (of starving).</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Ithpa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>אִסְתַּכֵּן</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to be exposed to danger, be hurt; to be in trouble</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. Y. Deut. XXV, 3. Targ. Ps. CXIX, 109.—Pes. 112
<sup>b</sup> וא' ליה and he might be injured; ib. ומִסְתַּכֵּן. Keth. 61
<sup>a</sup> אי לאו … אִסְתַּכְּנִי if he had not given it to me, I should have become seriously ill; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<entry id="O00926">
<head-word>סַכָּנָה</head-word>
<pos> f.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (סָכַן II) 
<italic>trouble, persecution, danger</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Keth. 3
<sup>b</sup> ומס' ואילך and since the days of danger (the Hadrianic persecution when the Romans enforced the jus primae noctis). Ib. האי ס' אונס הוא you call that risk of life (for religion’s sake)? This is rather assault (which no woman is bound to sacrifice her life in resisting). Ib. משום דאיכא צנועות … ואתיין לידי ס' because there are chaste women who would rather suffer death, and their lives might be endangered. Succ. 14
<sup>b</sup>; Sabb. 21
<sup>b</sup>, a. fr. בשעת הס' in times of religious persecution. Y. Shebi. I, 52
<sup>d</sup> top מעות של ס' coins of the revolution (confiscated coins). Bets. 22
<sup>a</sup> סַכָּנַת נפשות risk of life (serious illness). Ib. דבר שיש בו ס' a case of serious sickness; Succ. 26
<sup>a</sup> חולה שיש בו ס'. Y. Ab. Zar. II, 40
<sup>c</sup> top אופיון ס', v. אוּפְיוֹן. Ib., a. e. אהן סומקא ס' an inflammation of the eye is a case of serious illness (with regard to breaking the Sabbath laws); a. v. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="O00935">
<head-word>סִכְסֵךְ</head-word>
<hw-number>I</hw-number>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<language-reference>
<xref rid="O00904"> Pilp. of סָכַךְ I)</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be caught; to stick</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Nidd. 25
<sup>b</sup> מביא … אם מְסַכְסֵךְ וכ' one takes a chip with a smooth head and introduces it at the place of the genitals (of a miscarried foetus), and if it gets caught (that it can proceed no farther), it is sure to be a male foetus.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to</italic>
<italic>entangle, snare</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Gen. R. s. 67 ועופות ומְסַכְסְבָן וכ' and (he hunted) birds and ensnared them, but an angel came and freed them; Yalk. Prov. 950.—Part. f. מְסַכְסֶכֶת (sub. סַכִּין) 
<italic>a slaughtering knife having an indentation which catches the nail passing in one direction</italic>, contrad. to אוגרת which catches the nail in either direction. Ḥull. 17
<sup>b</sup> Ar. (ed. מְסוּכְסֶכֶת 
<italic>part. pass</italic>.).</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="O00936">
<head-word>סִכְסֵךְ</head-word>
<hw-number>II</hw-number>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (transpos. of כִּסְכֵּס; cmp. גִּעְגֵּעַ; v. 
<xref rid="K00949">כָּסַס</xref>) 
<italic>to chew, nibble</italic>; (of fire, cmp. לָחַךְ) 
<italic>to graze, singe, make brittle</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Sabb. 21

<entry id="O01015">
<head-word>סֶלַע</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> Arab. 
<italic>salʿa, to cleave</italic>) </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>rock, clod, boulder</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Tosef. B. Bath. I, 1 בס' הבא בידים if there is (between the two pits) a clod which crumbles under one’s hands; B. Bath. 17
<sup>b</sup>; 19
<sup>a</sup>. Orl. I, 3 אילן שנעקר והס' עמו if a tree has been uprooted with the clod on its roots; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. סְלָעִים, סְלָעִין</plural-form>. B. Bath. II, 1 מרחיקין … את הס' וכ' deposits of stones (or earth) must be kept off the neighbor’s wall &c.; Y. Sabb. IV, 6
<sup>d</sup> bot. לא שהס' מרתיחין וכ' not because they generate heat, but because they generate mould and ruin the wall. B. Bath. l. c. תנא הכא ס' והוא הדין לחול the Mishnah mentions stones and implies sand. Tanḥ. Ḥuck. 20 ס' כמין שדים rocks protruding like breasts; a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>pl.</italic> as ab.</definition>
<notes>
<italic>scales</italic> on the bodies of serpents. Tanḥ. M’tsorʿa 2 הס' שהן על הנחש וכ' the scales on the serpent’s back are its leprosy.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition>
<italic>Sela, a weight</italic> and 
<italic>a coin</italic> equal to one sacred or two common Shekels (v. Zuckerm. Talm. Münz., pp. 9; 24).</definition>
<notes> Kel. XII, 7 ס' שנפסלה וכ' a Sela which has been unfitted (as a coin) and which has been fitted up for use as a weight. Bekh. 50
<sup>a</sup> ס' של קדש וכ' the sacred S. contains 48 dupondia. Ib. כל כסף האמור בתורה סתם ס' every silver piece mentioned in the Pentateuch without any qualification means a S. Ib.
<sup>b</sup> (ref. to B. Kam. VIII, 6) ולא תימא ס' ארבע זוזי וכ' think not that the Mishnah means a S. of four Zuz, but it means half a Zuz, for people call half a Zuz a Sela (split, cmp. בֶּקַע); B. Kam. 36
<sup>b</sup> ס' צורי a Tyrian S.; ס' מדינה a country S. (one eighth of a Tyrian S., half a Zuz; v. supra); a. v. fr.—In gen. 
<italic>coin</italic>. Sabb. VI, 6 ס' שעל הצינית a coin placed on a sore of the foot. Ab. Zar. 54
<sup>b</sup> ס' שלי my (the Lord’s) coin (divine image of man), v. פּוּמְבִּי.—
<plural-form>Pl. as ab. Y. Sabb. l. c. תיפתר בס' של כסף</plural-form> it means 
<italic>s’laʿim</italic> (coins) of silver; בשל זהב וכ' golden, copper 
<italic>s’laʿim</italic>. Keth. V, 9 משקל חמשה ס' שתי וכ' warp of the weight of five S. in Judæa which is equal to ten S. in Galilee &c. Y. Kidd. I, 59
<sup>d</sup> bot., a. e. כל שקלים … ס' all Shekels mentioned in the Pentateuch mean S., v. supra; a. fr.—[Tosef. Ukts. I, 2 (T’bul Yom III) ס' של שבלים, v. מֵלַע.]</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="O01078">
<head-word>סמי</head-word>
<head-word>סָמָא</head-word>
<head-word>סָמָה</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (v. 
<xref rid="O00334">סוּם II</xref>) 
<italic>to tie up, close; to make blind</italic>.</definition>
<notes>—Part. pass. סָמוּי; f. סְמוּיָה, סְמוּיָיה; 
<plural-form>pl. סְמוּיִים, סְמוּיִין; סְמוּיוֹת</plural-form>
<italic>a</italic>) 
<italic>tied up, hidden</italic> (cmp. סִימָה). Taan. 8
<sup>b</sup> (ref. to אסמיך, Deut. XXVIII, 8) דבר הס' מן העין that which is hidden from sight (the exact quantity of which you do not know); B. Mets. 42
<sup>a</sup>; a. e.—
<italic>b</italic>) 
<italic>blinded, blind</italic>. Kidd. 24
<sup>b</sup> הרי שהיתה עינו ס' וכ' if the slave’s eye was blind, and he (the master) cut it out. Keth. 105
<sup>a</sup> כמה ס' עיניהם וכ' how blind are the eyes of (how short-sighted are) those who receive bribes!</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pi.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>סִמֵּא, סִימֵּא</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to blind, make blind</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Kidd. l. c. סי' עובר וכ' he injured the eye of the embryo (while operating on the mother). Ib. הרי שהיתה … וסִמְּאָהּ suppose the slave’s eye was dim, and he (the master) made it entirely blind. Y. Kil. VIII, 31
<sup>c</sup> top וסִימְּיָיהּ; B. Kam. 91
<sup>a</sup> וסִימְּאוֹ (Ms. M. וסימאה) and he made him blind. Ib. VIII, 7 האומר סַמֵּא וכ' if one says (to his neighbor), blind my eye, the neighbor is responsible. Gen. R. s. 75, end לו … לסַמּוֹת וכ' שלח he sent him a present in order to blind his eyes (with ref. to Deut. XVI, 19). Sabb. 109
<sup>a</sup> top יד מְסַמְּאָה an unwashed hand put on the eye makes blind. Gen. R. s. 42 (ref. to עין משפט, Gen. XIV, 7 עין … לסַמּוֹתָהּ they wanted to blind the eye (of him) that established the rule of justice in the world; a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to tie up one’s own eyes; to simulate blindness</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Tosef. Peah IV, 14; Y. ib. VIII, 21
<sup>b</sup> top; Keth. 68
<sup>a</sup> המְסמֵּא את עינו (a beggar) who ties his eye up.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Nif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>נִסְמָא, נִסְמָה</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to be blinded; to become blind</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Num. R. s. 7, beg. Bekh. V, 5 (36
<sup>b</sup>) שנִסְמֵת עינו (Talm. ed. שנִסְמֵית) that became blind on one eye; Keth. 77
<sup>a</sup> נִיסְמֵת; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hithpa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִסְתַּמֵּא, </binyan-form>
<binyan-name>Nithpa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>נִסְתַּמֵּא, נִסְתַּמָּה</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition />
<notes> same. Arakh. 17
<sup>b</sup>, sq. פִּתֵּחַ ונ' if he was open-eyed and became blind; B. Bath. 128
<sup>a</sup>. Num. R. s. 18 מיד היה מִסְתַּמֵּא (not היתה) he would get blind at once; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<sup>a</sup> אֲסַמְּיָיהּ; B. Kam. 91
<sup>b</sup>; a. e.—Sabb. 52

<sup>b</sup>. Lev. R. s. 22 ואִיסְתַּמְיַת and she became blind. Ib. דין דהוה פתיח א' he who was open-eyed got blind; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<italic>s’mikhah</italic> (on the Holy Days). Snh. I, 3 סְמִיכַת זקנים the laying on of hands by the elders (Lev. IV, 15); Tosef. ib. I, 1, v. next w. Y. ib. I, 19

<plural-form>Pl. סְמִיכוֹת</plural-form>. Kidd. I, 8. Men. 88

<entry id="O01097">
<head-word>סָמַךְ</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (b. h.) [
<italic>to close, join</italic>,] </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to pack, make close, stamp.</italic></definition>
<notes> Shebi. III, 8 לא יִסְמוֹךְ בעפר one should not support the dam by packing earth upon it, v. סָבַךְ. Gen. R. s. 5 סְמָבָן וכ' he crowded them between &c. (Lev. R. s. 10 שָׂמָן); a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to support, stem</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Midr. Till. to Ps. CXXXVI, עוג היה … וסוֹמְכוֹ Og broke a mountain loose and threw it on the Israelites …, Moses took a pebble and mentioned the Holy Name over it and stemmed its fall; הידים שכך סוֹמְכוֹת the hands which thus stem (the mountain); Deut. R. s. 1, end; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to bring close, to join</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Y. Sabb. III, 5
<sup>d</sup> bot. אפי' לִסְמוֹךְ לו even to place a vessel close to it (to be warmed); Bab. ib. 38
<sup>b</sup>. Y. Kil. II, 27
<sup>d</sup> סוֹמְכִין עומרין וכ' you may put packed sheaves by the side of &c. Kil. II, 7 לסמוך לו וכ' to plant closely adjoining to it &c. Ib. 8; a. fr.—Esp. (sub. יד) a) 
<italic>to press hands on the head of a sacrifice</italic> (to indicate ownership). Men. IX, 8 הכל סוֹמְכִין וכ' all persons are entitled to lay hands on their sacrifices, except &c. Ḥag. II, 2 שלא לסמוך that the laying on of hands must not be done on the Holy Days. Ib. 3 ואין סומכין עליהם but hands must not be laid on them; a. fr.—b) 
<italic>to lay hands on the head of a scholar</italic>, in gen. 
<italic>to ordain</italic>. Snh. 14
<sup>a</sup> the government decreed שכל הסומך יהרג וכ' that whosoever ordained a scholar should be put to death, and whosoever be ordained should be put to death, ועיר שסומכין וכ' and the town wherein the ordination takes place &c. Ib. וס' שם חמשה וכ' and he ordained there five elders. Ib. ר"מ לא סְמָכוֹ ר"ע that R. Akiba never ordained R. M.—Ib. סומכין בארץ ונִסְמָכִין וכ' if those ordaining stand on Palestinean ground, and 
<pgbrk id="pg1001" />those to be ordained outside of Palestine; a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—4)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to lean, to rely</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ber. 9
<sup>a</sup>, a. fr., v. כְּדָיי. Erub. 65
<sup>b</sup> נִסְמוֹךְ על וכ' let us rely on the opinion of &c.; a. fr.—Trnsf. a) 
<italic>to support; to find support for an opinion</italic> or 
<italic>a rule</italic>, (v. אַסְמַכְתָּא). Y. Shebi. X, 39
<sup>c</sup> bot. (ref. to Deut. XV, 3) מיכן סָמְכוּ לפרוזבול וכ' here they found a support for the 
<italic>prosbol</italic> as a Biblical institution, expl. בשהתקין הלל סְמָכוּהוּ וכ' when Hillel had instituted it, they supported it by reference to &c.—b) (with ענין) 
<italic>to bring under the same rule laws which are joined in the Biblical text</italic>. Yeb. 4
<sup>a</sup> (ref. to Ex. XXII, 17 a. 18) סמכו עניין לו וכ' they brought the subject (verse 17) close to it (verse 18) (to intimate) as the punishment for the one is stoning, so is it for the other. Ib. וכי מפני שסמכו וכ' can we put a person to death on an intimation suggested merely by the neighborhood of two subjects? (v. סְמוּכִים, infra).—
<italic>Part. pass</italic>. סָמוּךְ; f. סְמוּכָה; 
<plural-form>pl. סְמוּכִים, סְמוּכִין; סְמוּכוֹת</plural-form> a) 
<italic>near, close by</italic>. Meg. 3
<sup>b</sup> וכל הס' לו and all (the inhabited area) adjoining it. Men. 98
<sup>a</sup>, a. e. על בס' the preposition 
<italic>ʿ</italic>
<italic>al</italic> means 
<italic>immediately on</italic>. Sifré Num. 131 הרבה פרשיות ס' וכ' many sections (in the Torah) adjoin one another, and yet are (mentally) as far from one another &c. Sabb. I, 2 ס' למנחה near Minḥah time; a. v. fr.—Esp. סְמוּכִין, סְמוּכִים 
<italic>the interpretation founded on the fact of local junction of texts</italic> (v. supra). Yeb. l. c. ס' מן התורה מנין where is it intimated that Biblical texts are to be interpreted on the basis of proximity? Answ. (ref. to Ps. CXI, 8): they are arranged &c. Ib. מאן דלא דריש ס' he who does not adopt the interpretation based on textual proximity. Ber. 10
<sup>a</sup>; a. fr.—b) 
<italic>strong</italic>, 
<italic>hardened</italic>. Num. R. s. 9 לבה ס' עליהם her heart is hardened towards them (and their presence will prevent her from confessing her guilt); cmp. גּוּס I.</notes></sense></senses>

<binyan-name>Nif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>נִסְמַךְ</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be adjoined</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ber. l. c. למה נִסְמְכָה וכ' why has the section referring to Absalom (Ps. III) been joined to that relating to Gog and Magog (Ps. II)? Tanḥ. Ḥuck. 20 ונ' להר וכ' and is close to the mountain opposite. M. Kat. 28
<sup>a</sup>; a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be ordained</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Snh. l. c., v. supra. Yoma 87
<sup>a</sup> שראויין לִיסָּמֵךְ who are worthy to be ordained; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pi.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>סִימֵּךְ</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to support</italic>, 
<italic>prop.</italic> Y. Maasr. II, 50
<sup>a</sup> top המְסַמֵּךְ בגפנים he who props vines.</definition>
<notes> Yalk. Ex. 244 עוזר ומסמך אתה וכ' thou art a helper and supporter to all &c.; a. e.—Part. pass. מְסוּמָּךְ, 
<plural-form>pl. מְסוּמָּכִין</plural-form>. Kel. II, 2 יושבין שלא מ' (vessels or fragments of vessels) resting without the need of a support.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִסְמִיךְ</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to pack, tread</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Y. Maasr. l. c. ברגליו מַסְמִיךְ working with his feet is he who packs (sheaves &c.; Y. B. Mets. VII, beg. 11
<sup>b</sup> מקמץ).</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hithpa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִסְתַּמֵּךְ, </binyan-form>
<binyan-name>Nithpa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>נִסְתַּמֵּךְ</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to lean one’s self</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Gen. R. s. 45, end היתה מִסְתַּמֶּכֶת על וכ' was leaning on her handmaid. Sifré Num. 131 והיה מִסְתַּמֵּךְ וכ' and he went off leaning on his stick; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<senses>
<sense>

<sup>a</sup>; a. e.—Esp. 
<italic>to ordain</italic> (v. preced., a. Targ. Deut. XXXIV, 9). Snh. 13

<sup>a</sup> ור"מ … סַמְכֵיה was it R. J. ben B. that ordained R. Meir? Ib. הוה מיטמר מלמיסמכיה Ms. M. was on his guard not to be ordained. Ib. סְמוֹכוּ לנא appoint for us as teachers, v. חֲמִיסִין; a. fr.—
<italic>Part. pass.</italic> סָמִיךְ, סְמִיךְ a) 
<italic>ordained</italic>. Pes. 49
<sup>a</sup> תרי בני סְמִיכֵי two sons both of whom were ordained teachers.—b) 
<italic>near</italic>, 
<italic>adjoining</italic>. Targ. Y. I Num. XXI, 14. Ib. II, 5; 12, a. e. (interch. with סְמוּכִין). Targ. Y. Deut. VI, 7.—Snh. 7

<sup>a</sup>; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses>

<sup>c</sup>; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
